label: tree
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{tree}
Among all trees on n vertices, the maximum eccentric subgraph index is attained by the star and the minimum eccentric subgraph index is attained by the path.
head: environment

label: edge
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{edge}
Let $G$ be a graph and let $u, v \in V(G)$ be two non-adjacent vertices. Let $\tilde{G}$ be the graph obtained from $G$ by joining $u$ and $v$ with an edge. Then $ES(G)<ES(\tilde{G})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $e=\{u,v\}$ be the edge of $\tilde{G}$ joining $u$ and $v$. For $x\in V(\tilde{G})$, $\epsilon_{\tilde{G}}(x)=f_{\tilde{G}}(x,w)$ for some $w\in V(\tilde{G})$. 
We have $f_{\tilde{G}}(x,w)=f_{\tilde{G}}^{e+}(x,w)+ f_{\tilde{G}}^{e-}(x,w)$, where $f_{\tilde{G}}^{e+}(x,w)$ is the number of connected subgraph of $\tilde{G}$ 
containing $x$, $w$ and the edge $e$ and $f_{\tilde{G}}^{e-}(x,w)$ is the number of connected subgraph of $\tilde{G}$ containing $x$, $w$ but not the edge $e$. Since $f_{\tilde{G}}^{e-}(x,w)=f_{G}(x,w)$ and $f_{\tilde{G}}^{e+}(x,w)>0$, we have $\epsilon_{\tilde{G}}(x)>f_{G}(x,w)\geq \epsilon_{G}(x)$. Thus $$ES(\tilde{G})=\displaystyle\sum_{x\in V(\tilde{G})}\epsilon_{\tilde{G}}(x)>\displaystyle\sum_{x\in V(G)}\epsilon_{G}(x)=ES(G).$$
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm1}
Among all graphs on $n$ vertices, the eccentric subgraph index is maximized by the complete graph $K_n$  and minimized by the path $P_n$.

label: thm2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm2}
Let $G$ and $G'$ be the graphs mentioned in Lemma \ref{lem1} (Figure \ref{fig1}). If $G_1$ is a tree then $ES(G)<ES(G')$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $G_1$ and $G'_2$ be the subgraphs  of $G'$ such that $G_1\cup G'_2=G'$ and $V(G_1)\cap V(G'_2)=\{v_1\}$. Suppose $\epsilon_{G'}(v_2)=f_{G'}(v_2,s)$. We have two cases here.\\
{\bf Case-I:} $s\in V(G_1)$\\
In this case, we have 
\begin{align*} 
 \epsilon_{G}(v_2)\leq f_{G}(v_2,s)&=f_{G_2}(v_2)f_{G_1}(v_1,s)\\
                                   &=f_{G'_2}(v_2,v_1)f_{G_1}(v_1,s)\\
                                   &=f_{G'}(v_2,s)\\
                                   &=\epsilon_{G'}(v_2).
\end{align*}
 Now the result follows from Lemma \ref{lem1}.
 
\noindent {\bf Case-II:} $s\in V(G'_2)\setminus v_2$ \\
In this case,
$f_{G'}(v_2,s)=f_{G'_2}(v_2,s)f_{G_1}(v_1)=f_{G_2}(v_2,s)f_{G_1}(v_1)$, $f_{G'}(v_1,s)=f_{G'_2}(v_1,s)f_{G_1}(v_1)=2f_{G_2}(v_2,s)f_{G_1}(v_1)$,
  $f_{G}(v_2,s)=f_{G_2}(v_2,s)(1+f_{G_1}(v_1))$    and  $f_{G}(v_1,s)=f_{G_2}(v_2,s)f_{G_1}(v_1).$ Thus
\begin{align*}
   &f_{G}(v_1,s)+f_{G}(v_2,s)= f_{G_2}(v_2,s)(1+2f_{G_1}(v_1)),\\
   &f_{G'}(v_1,s)+f_{G'}(v_2,s)=3f_{G_2}(v_2,s)f_{G_1}(v_1).
\end{align*}
Since $G_1$ is a tree,  by Lemma $\ref{lem3}$,  we have $\epsilon_{G'}(v_1)=f_{G'}(v_1,s)$. Hence,
\begin{align*}
    \epsilon_{G}(v_{1})+\epsilon_{G}(v_2)\leq f_{G}(v_2,s)+f_{G}(v_1,s) <f_{G'}(v_1,s)+f_{G'}(v_2,s)= \epsilon_{G'}(v_1)+\epsilon_{G'}(v_2),
\end{align*}
and the result follows from Lemma $\ref{lem1}$.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: Among all trees on $n$ vertices, the star $K_{1,n-1}$ has the maximum eccentric subgraph index.
head: environment

title: Conjecture
body_md:
Let $G$ be a graph with a cut edge $e=\{v_1,v_2\}$. Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be the  connected components of $G-e$ containing $v_1$ and $v_2$, respectively, with 
$|V(G_i)|\geq 2$ for $i=1,2$. Let $G'$ be the graph obtained from $G$ by identifying $v_1$ and $v_2$ and adding a pendant  vertex $v_2$  at the identified vertex  $v_{1}$. Then $ES(G)< ES(G').$
head: environment

label: prop1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop1}
Let $C_n:v_1v_2 \cdots v_nv_1$ be the cycle on $n\geq 3$ vertices. Then $\epsilon_{C_n}(v_i)=\lfloor \frac{n^2+2n+5}{4}\rfloor$ for $i=1,2,\ldots,n$. Furthermore, $ES(C_n)=n\lfloor \frac{n^2+2n+5}{4}\rfloor$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since all vertices of $C_n$ have the same eccentric subgraph number,  we will only compute $\epsilon(v_1)=\min\{f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k),\ 2\leq k\leq n\}$. Observe that $C_n$ itself a connected subgraph containing $v_1$ and $v_k$ and  all other connected subgraphs  of $C_n$ containing $v_1$ and $v_k$ are the paths containing $v_1$ and $v_k$. There are exactly two paths of $C_n$ containing both $v_1$ and $v_k$ as  pendant vertices, one  is $v_1v_2 \cdots v_k$ and another is $v_kv_{k+1} \cdots v_nv_{1}$. Also, we have $2(n-k)+2(k-2)=2(n-2)$ paths of $C_n$ containing both $v_1$ and $v_k$, and either $v_1$ or $v_k$ as a pendant vertex. The number of paths of $C_n$ containing both $v_1$ and $v_k$ as non-pendant vertices is $\binom{n-k}{2}+\binom{k-2}{2}$. Thus $f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)=3+2(n-2)+\binom{n-k}{2}+\binom{k-2}{2}=2n-1+\binom{n-k}{2}+\binom{k-2}{2}$. So,
\begin{align*}
  f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)- f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{k+1})&=\left[\binom{n-k}{2}-\binom{n-k-1}{2}\right]-\left[\binom{k-1}{2}-\binom{k-2}{2}\right] \\
   &=\binom{n-k-1}{1}-\binom{k-2}{1} \\
   &=n-2k+1.
\end{align*}
Hence, $f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)> f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{k+1})$  if $k<\frac{n+1}{2}$ and $f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)< f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{k+1})$ if $k>\frac{n+1}{2}$.

Suppose $n$ is even. Then $f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)> f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{k+1})$  if  $k\leq \frac{n}{2}$ and $f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)< f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{k+1})$  if    $k\geq \frac{n}{2}+1$. So, $\epsilon_{C_n}(v_1)=f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{\frac{n}{2}+1})=\frac{n^2+2n+4}{4}$.
Suppose $n$ is odd. Then $f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)> f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{k+1})$  if  $k\leq \frac{n-1}{2}$ and $f_{C_n}(v_1,v_k)< f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{k+1})$  if    $k\geq \frac{n+3}{2}$. So, $\epsilon_{C_n}(v_1)=f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{\frac{n+1}{2}})=f_{C_n}(v_1,v_{\frac{n+3}{2}})=\frac{n^2+2n+5}{4}$.  Thus,  $\epsilon_{C_n}(v_i)=\lfloor \frac{n^2+2n+5}{4}\rfloor$ for $i=1,2,\ldots,n$ and hence $ES(C_n)=n\lfloor \frac{n^2+2n+5}{4}\rfloor$.
head: environment

label: lem4
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem4}
Let $C_n:v_1v_2 \cdots v_nv_1$ be the cycle on $n\geq 3$ vertices. Then $f_{C_n}(v_i)= 2n +\binom{n-1}{2}$ for $i=1,2,\ldots,n.$
head: environment

label: lem5
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem5}
Let $U_{n,g}(T_1,T_2,\dots,T_g)\in \mathcal{U}_{n,g}$ with $|V(T_i)|=n_i+1$ for $i=1,2,\ldots ,g $. Then $ES(U_{n,g}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_g))\leq ES(U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g}))$ where $v_i$ is the center of $K_{1,n_i}$ and the equality happens if and only if $T_i\cong K_{1,n_i}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: If $T_i$ is not a star for some $i$, then the vertex $v_i$ is adjacent to a vertex $v$  of $T_i$ with $deg(v)\geq 2$. Identify the vertices $v$ and $v_i$, and add $v$ as a pendant vertex at the identified vertex  $v_{i}$. Repeat this process until $T_i$ becomes $K_{1,n_i}$ with center $v_i$. By Theorem $\ref{thm2}$, the eccentric subgraph index will increase in each step. Continuing this process, we  get $ES(U_{n,g}(T_1,T_2,\dots,T_g))\leq ES(U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g}))$ and equality occurs  if and only if $T_i\cong K_{1,n_i}$ for each $1\leq i\leq g$.
head: environment

label: lem6
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: thm3
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm3}
Let $G\in \mathcal{U}_{n,g}$. Then $ES(G)\leq ES(U^p_{n,g})$ and the equality happens if and only if $G\cong U^p_{n,g}.$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The result is obvious if $n-g= 0$ or $1$. So, assume that $n-g\geq 2$. Let $G=U_{n,g}(T_1,T_2,\dots,T_g)\in \mathcal{U}_{n,g}$ with $|V(T_i)|=n_i+1$($n_i\geq 0$) for $i=1,2,\ldots ,g $. Then by by Lemma $\ref{lem5}$,  we have $\epsilon(G))\leq\epsilon(U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\ldots,K_{1,n_g}))$ and the equality occurs  if and only if $T_i\cong K_{1,n_i}$ with $v_i$ is the center of $K_{1,n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq g$.

W.l.o.g., take $n_1\geq n_2\geq \cdots \geq n_g$. We have  $U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\ldots,K_{1,n_g}) \cong U^p_{n,g}$ if and only if $n_1=n-g$. Suppose $n_1\neq n-g$. Then there exists a vertex $v_k\neq v_1$ such that  $deg(v_k)\geq 3$.  We can obtain $U^p_{n,g}$ from $U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})$ by deleting all the pendant vertices of $U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})$ and adding them as pendant vertices at $v_1$. It is enough to show that $\epsilon(U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g}))<\epsilon(U^p_{n,g})$.

  
By Lemma $\ref{lem6}$, for any $v\in V(U^p_{n,g})$, we have  $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(v)=f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v,x)$, where $x$ is a pendant vertex of $U^p_{n,g}$. Let $y$ be a pendant vertex at $v_1$ in $U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})$. Then

\begin{align*}
  \epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1)= f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1,y)=2^{(n-g-1)}f_{C_g}(v_1)=2^{(n-g-1)}f_{C_g}(v_1,v_k)+2^{(n-g-1)}f_{C_g}(v_1,\overline{v_k}). 
\end{align*}
 Since $$f_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(v_1,\overline{v_k},y)<2^{(n-g-1)}f_{C_g}(v_1,\overline{v_k})$$
  and $f_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(v_1,v_k,y)\leq 2^{(n-g-1)}f_{C_g}(v_1,v_k)$ (with equality happens if and only if $n_1+n_k=n-g$), 
\begin{align*}
  \epsilon_{{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}}(v_1)\leq  f_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(v_1,y)< f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1,y)=\epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1).
\end{align*}
For $2\leq i \leq g$, we have $f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_i,y)=2^{(n-g-1)}f_{C_g}(v_i,v_1)$ and so
 $$ \epsilon_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(v_i)\leq f_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(v_i,y)\leq f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_i,y)=\epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_i)$$ where second inequality becomes equality if and only if $n_1+n_i=n-g$.
 
Now let $z$ be a pendant vertex  of $U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})$ adjacent to $v_j$ for some $j$. Then $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(z)=f_{U^p_{n,g}}(z,x)=2^{n-g-2}f_{C_g}(v_1)$ where $x\neq z$ is a pendant vertex of $U^p_{n,g}$. So, $$\epsilon_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(z)\leq f_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(z,x)< f_{U^p_{n,g}}(z,x)=\epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(z).$$ 

Thus $\epsilon_{U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g})}(v)\leq \epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(v)$ for all vertex $v$, with strict inequality atleast at one vertex. Hence, $\epsilon(U_{n,g}(K_{1,n_1},K_{1,n_2},\dots,K_{1,n_g}))<\epsilon(U^p_{n,g})$ and this proves the result.
head: environment

label: lem7
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem7}
Let $n\geq 5$ and $4\leq g < n$. Then $ES(U^p_{n,g})<ES(U^p_{n,{g-1}})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let  $C_g:v_1v_2\cdots v_gv_1$ be the cycle in $U^p_{n,g}$ with  all $n-g$ pendant vertices attached to $v_1$. Obtain $U^p_{n,g-1}$ form $U^p_{n,g}$ by identifying the vertices $v_g$ and $v_1$ as $v_1$ and adding $v_g$ as a pendant vertex at $v_1$. Let $y$ be a pendant vertex at $v_1$ in both $U^p_{n,g}$ and $U^p_{n,g-1}$. Then 
 
 $$f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1,y)=2^{n-g-1} \left(2g+\binom{g-1}{2}\right)\;\; \mbox{and} \;\; f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_1,y)=2^{n-g} \left(2g-2+\binom{g-2}{2}\right),$$ also 

  $$f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_g,y)=2^{n-g-1}\left(2g-1+\binom{g-2}{2}\right)\;\; \mbox{and} \;\; f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_g,y)=2^{n-g-1}\left(2(g-1)+\binom{g-2}{2}\right).$$

So, $f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1,y)+f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_g,y)=2^{n-g-1}\left(4g-1+\binom{g-1}{2}+\binom{g-2}{2}\right)=2^{n-g-1}(g^2+3)$ and 
\begin{align*}
f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_1,y)+f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_g,y)&=2^{n-g-1}\left(6(g-1)+3\binom{g-2}{2}\right)\\
                                                 &>2^{n-g-1}(6(g-1)+(g-2)(g-3))\\
                                                 &=2^{n-g-1}(g^2+g).
\end{align*}
By Lemma $\ref{lem6}$, we have $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_1)=f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_1,y)$ and $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_g)=f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_g,y)$ and thus
\begin{align*} 
\epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1)+\epsilon_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_g)&\leq f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_1,y)+f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_g,y)\\
                                                   &=2^{n-g-1}(g^2+3)\\
                                                   &< 2^{n-g-1}(g^2+g)\\
                                                   &<f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_1,y)+f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_g,y)\\
                                                   &=\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_1)+\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_g).
\end{align*} 


For $2\leq j\leq g-1$, we have 
$$ f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_j,y)=2^{n-g-1}\left(2g-1+\binom{g-j}{2}+\binom{j-2}{2}\right)$$  and 
$$f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_j,y)=2^{n-g}\left(2(g-1)-1+\binom{g-1-j}{2}+\binom{j-2}{2}\right).$$ So,
\begin{align*}
    f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_j,y)-f_{U^p_{n,g}}(v_j,y)&=2^{n-g-1}\left(2g-5+2\binom{g-1-j}{2}-\binom{g-j}{2}+\binom{j-2}{2}\right)\\
                                                 &=2^{n-g-1}\left(2g-5+\binom{g-j-1}{2}-\binom{g-j}{2}+\binom{g-j-1}{2}+\binom{j-2}{2}\right)\\
                                                 &=2^{n-g-1}\left(2g-5-(g-j-1)+\binom{g-j-1}{2}+\binom{j-2}{2}\right)\\
                                                 &=2^{n-g-1}\left(g+j-4+\binom{g-j-1}{2}+\binom{j-2}{2}\right)\\
                                                 &>0\;\; \mbox{(since $g\geq 4$  and $j\geq 2$)}.
\end{align*}
Thus, $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g}}}(v_j)\leq  f_{U^p_{n,{g}}}(v_j,y)<f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_j,y)=\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(v_j)$ for $2\leq j \leq g-1$.\\

Let $x$ be a pendant vertex of $U^p_{n,{g}}$. If $n-g\geq 2$ then by Lemma $\ref{lem6}$, we have $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g}}}(x)=f_{U^p_{n,{g}}}(x,y)$ for some pendant vertex $y\neq x$. So, $f_{U^p_{n,g}}(x,y)=2^{n-g-2} (2g+\binom{g-1}{2})$ and $f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(x,y)=2^{n-g-1} (2g-2+\binom{g-2}{2})$. Thus 
\begin{align*}
   f_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(x,y)-f_{U^p_{n,g}}(x,y)&=2^{n-g-2}\left(2g-4+2\binom{g-2}{2}-\binom{g-1}{2}\right)\\
   &=2^{n-g-2}\left(2g-4+\binom{g-2}{2}-\binom{g-1}{2}+\binom{g-2}{2}\right)\\
   &=2^{n-g-2}\left(2g-4-(g-2)+\binom{g-2}{2}\right)\\
   &=2^{n-g-2}\left(g-2+\binom{g-2}{2}\right)>0  \;\; \mbox{(since $g\geq 4$)}.
\end{align*}
So, $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g}}}(x)<\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(x)$ if $n-g\geq 2$.

If $n-g=1$ then $x=y$. By Lemma $\ref{lem6}$, we have $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g}}}(x)=f_{U^p_{n,g}}(x,v_{\lfloor \frac{g+2}{2} \rfloor})$ and  $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(x)=f_{U^p_{n,g-1}}(x,v_g)=2(g-1)+\binom{g-2}{2}$. If $g$ is even  
\begin{align*}
 f_{U^p_{n,g-1}}(x,v_g)-f_{U^p_{n,g}}(x,v_{\lfloor \frac{g+2}{2} \rfloor})= \frac{g^2-g+2}{2}-\frac{g^2+2g+4}{4}=\frac{g^2-4g}{4}\geq 0,\; \mbox{(since $g\geq 4$)},
\end{align*}
 and if $g$ is odd 
\begin{align*}
 f_{U^p_{n,g-1}}(x,v_g)-f_{U^p_{n,g}}(x,v_{\lfloor \frac{g+2}{2} \rfloor})= \frac{g^2-g+2}{2}-\frac{g^2+2g+5}{4}=\frac{g^2-4g-1}{4}>0,\; \mbox{(since $g\geq 5$)}.
\end{align*}
Thus $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g}}}(x)\leq\epsilon_{U^p_{n,{g-1}}}(x)$ and this proves the result.
head: environment

label: lem8
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For $n=4$, there is single pendant vertex $x$ at $v_1$. Then $\epsilon_{U^p_{4,3}}(v_1)=7$, $\epsilon_{U^p_{4,3}}(v_2)=\epsilon_{U^p_{4,3}}(v_3)=5$ and $\epsilon_{U^p_{4,3}}(x)=f_{U^p_{4,3}}(x,v_2)=5$. So, $ES({U^p_{n,3}})=22$. For $n\geq 5$, $U^p_{n,3}$  has $n-3\geq 2$ pendant vertices attached to $v_1$. Then $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,3}}(v_1)=7\times2^{n-4}$ and $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,3}}(v_2)=\epsilon_{U^p_{n,3}}(v_3)=5\times2^{n-4}$. Also, for any  pendant vertex $x$ at $v_1$,   $\epsilon_{U^p_{n,3}}(x)=7\times2^{n-5}$. Thus, $ES({U^p_{n,3}})=7\times2^{n-4}+2\times5\times2^{n-4}+(n-3)\times7\times2^{n-5}=2^{n-5}(13+7n)$.

label: rem1
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem1}
From  Proposition  $\ref{prop1}$, we have, $ES(C_4)=28$  and $ES(C_5)=50$. Hence,  $ES(U^p_{4,3})<ES(C_4)$ and also $ES(U^p_{5,3})<ES(C_5)$.
head: environment

label: thm4
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm4}
 Let $G$ be a unicyclic graph on $n\geq 6$ vertices. Then $ES(G)\leq ES(U^p_{n,3})$ and the equality happens if and only if $G\cong U^p_{n,3}.$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
From Theorem $\ref{thm3}$ and Lemma $\ref{lem7}$, it follows that either $U^p_{n,3}$ or $C_n$ maximizes the eccentric subgraph index  among all  unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices. From  Proposition  $\ref{prop1}$ and  Lemma $\ref{lem8}$, we have $ES(C_n)=n\lfloor \frac{n^2+2n+5}{4}\rfloor$ and $ES({U^p_{n,3}})=2^{n-5}(13+7n)$. So,
\begin{align*}
  \epsilon(U^p_{n,3})-\epsilon(C_n)&=2^{n-5}(13+7n)-n\lfloor \frac{n^2+2n+5}{4}\rfloor\\
  &\geq 2^{n-5}(13+7n)- \frac{n^3+2n^2+5n}{4}\\
  &=\frac{2^{n-3}(13+7n)-(n^3+2n^2+5n)}{4}\\
  &=\frac{n(5\times2^{n-3}-n^2)+2(5\times2^{n-3}-n^2)+n(2\times2^{n-3}-5)+3\times 2^{n-3}}{4}\\
  &=\frac{(5\times2^{n-3}-n^2)(n+2)+n(2^{n-2}-5)+3\times 2^{n-3}}{4}>0,
\end{align*}
as $5\times2^{n-3}-n^2>0$ and $2^{n-2}-5>0$ for $n\geq 6$. This proves the result.

label: lem9
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem9}
Let $T\in\mathcal{T}^n_{d}$. If $T\notin C^n_d$ then there exist a $T'\in C^n_d$ such that $ES(T)<ES(T')$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let  $P_{d+1}:v_0v_1\cdots v_d$ be a path in $T$. For $1\leq i\leq d-1$, Let $X_i$ be the component of  $T-v_{i-1}v_i-v_iv_{i+1}$ containing $v_i$. If $T\notin C^n_d$  then there exists $j$, where $1\leq j\leq d-1$ such that $X_j$ is not a star with center at $v_j$. So, $v_j$ is adjacent to a vertex $v\in V(X_j)$ such that $deg(v)\geq 2$. Identify $v$ and $v_j$, and add $v$ as a pendant vertex at the identified vertex  $v_{j}$. Repeat this process until $X_j$ becomes  a star with center $v_j$. Continue this process till all $X_i$ are stars with center $v_i$. Call the new tree as $T'$. Clearly $T'\in C^n_d$. By Theorem $\ref{thm2}$, in each step  the eccentric subgraph index will increase and hence $ES(T)<ES(T')$.
head: environment

label: lem10
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem10}
Let $T\in C^n_d$ and let $P_{d+1}:v_0v_1\cdots v_d$ be a path in $T$. Then for  $v\in V(T)$,  $\epsilon_T(v)=min\{f_T(v,v_0), f_T(v,v_d)\}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the path $P_{d+1}:v_0v_1\cdots v_d$  in $T$. Then $v_0$ and $v_d$ are pendant vertices and  $f_T(v_0,v_d)=2^{n-d-1}$.
Let $x,y\in V(T)$ be two pendant vertices. Suppose $x$ and $y$ are adjacent to $v_i$ and $v_j$, respectively where $1\leq i
<j\leq d-1$. Let $X,Y$ and $Z$ be the components of $T-v_{i-1}v_{i}-v_jv_{j+1}$, with $v_{i-1}\in V(X)$, $v_i,v_j\in  V(Y)$ and $v_{j+1}\in V(Z)$.  We have $f_Y(x,y)=2^{n_i+\dots+n_j-2}$, $f_X(v_{i-1})=2^{n_{i-1}}+2^{{n_{i-1}+n_{i-2}}}+\dots+2^{n_{i-1}+\dots+n_1+1}$ and $f_Z(v_{j+1})=2^{n_{j+1}}+2^{n_{j+1}+n_{j+2}}+\dots+2^{n_{j+1}+\dots+n_{d-1}+1}$. Then
\begin{align*}
f_T(x,y)&=f_Y(x,y)(1+f_X(v_{i-1})+f_Z(v_{j+1})+f_X(v_{i-1})f_Z(v_{j+1}))\geq 2^{n_1+\dots+n_{d-1}}.
\end{align*}
So $f_T(v_0,v_d)\leq f_T(x,y)$. Hence, $\epsilon^d(T)=f_T(v_0,v_d)$ and  by Theorem $\ref{zha1}$(iii), we have  $\epsilon_T(v)=min\{f_T(v,v_0), f_T(v,v_d)\}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
\item [(i)] Let $d$ be even. Suppose $T$ is not isomorphic to $T^e_{n,d}$. We have two cases:\\
{\bf Case-I:} $T\in C^n_d$\\
Let $P_{d+1}:v_0v_1\cdots v_d$ be a path in $T$. W.l.o. g. we can take $deg_{T}(v_i)\geq 3$ for some $i$ where $1\leq i \leq \frac{d}{2} -1$ as $T$ is not isomorphic to $T^e_{n,d}$. We can get $T^e_{n,d}$  from $T$ by deleting all the pendant vertices of $T$ except $v_0$ and $v_d$ and attaching them as pendant vertices at $v_{\frac{d}{2}}$. Then $\epsilon_T(v_{\frac{d}{2}})\leq f_T(v_{\frac{d}{2}},v_d)< (k+1)2^{n-d-1}=\epsilon_{T^e_{n,d}}(v_{\frac{d}{2}})$. It can be checked that for any $x\in V(T)\setminus v_{\frac{d}{2}}$, $\epsilon_T(x)\leq \epsilon_{T^e_{n,d}}(x)$. Thus $ES(T)<ES(T^e_{n,d})$.\\
{\bf Case-II:} $T\notin C^n_d$\\
By Lemma \ref{lem9}, there exists a $T'\in C^n_d$ such that $ES(T)<ES(T')$ and then by Case-I, we have  $ES(T)<ES(T')\leq ES(T^e_{n,d})$.
Now the result follows from Remark \ref{rem3}.
\item [(ii)]  Let $d$ be odd. Suppose $T$ is not isomorphic to $T^{o(r,s)}_{n,d}$ for any $r,s\geq 0$ with $r+s=n-d-1$. Then similarly to (i), we can show that  $ES(T)<ES(T^{o(r,s)}_{n,d})$ for some $r,s\geq 0$ with $r+s=n-d-1$. Now the result follows from Remark \ref{rem4}.
\end{enumerate}

Let $G\in \mathcal{G}^k_n$. If $G\notin G^k_n(S)$ then there exist a $G'\in G^k_n(S)$ such that $ES(G)<ES(G')$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_{n-k}$ be the non-pendant vertices of $G$. Since $G\notin G^k_n(S)$, there exist $v_i$ and $v_j$ such that $v_i$ is not adjacent to $v_j$ in $G$. Obtain a new graph $G'$ from $G$ by joining  all such non-adjacent pair of vertices from the set $\{v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_{n-k}\}$. Then by Lemma \ref{edge}, $ES(G)<ES(G')$.

label: thm6
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm6}
Let $2\leq k\leq n-3$ and  let $G\in\mathcal{G}^k_n$. Then $ES(G)\leq ES(K^k_{n-k})$ and equality happens if and only if $G\cong K^k_{n-k}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $G$ is not isomorphic to $K^k_{n-k}$. We have two cases:\\
{\bf Case-I:} $G\in G^k_n(S)$\\
We can obtain $K^k_{n-k}$ from $G$ by deleting all the pendant vertices of $G$ and attaching them as pendant vertices to $v_1$.
Since $G$ is not isomorphic to $K^k_{n-k}$, for some $i\geq 2$ there exists a vertex $v_i$ in $G$ with degree at least $n-k$. Let $z$ be a pendant vertex adjacent to $v_i$ in $G$. Let $x$ be a pendant vertex adjacent to $v_1$ in $G$. Then $\epsilon_G(z)\leq f_G(z,x)\leq 2^{k-2}f_{K_{n-k}}(v_i,v_1)$. By Lemma \ref{lem14}(ii), we have $\epsilon_{K^k_{n-k}}(z)=\min\{f_{K^k_{n-k}}(z,x),f_{K^k_{n-k}}(z,v_i)\}=\min\{2^{k-2}f_{K_{n-k}}(v_1),2^{k-1}f_{K_{n-k}}(v_1,v_i)\}>2^{k-2}f_{K_{n-k}}(v_i,v_1)\geq \epsilon_G(z)$. Thus $\epsilon_G(z)<\epsilon_{K^k_{n-k}}(z)$. Also 
\begin{align*}
\epsilon_G(v_1)&\leq f_G(v_1,z)\leq 2^{k-1}f_{K_{n-k}}(v_1,v_i)\\
&< \min\{2^kf_{K_{n-k}}(v_1,v_i),2^{k-1}f_{K_{k-n}}(v_1)\}\\
&=\min\{f_{K^k_{n-k}}(v_1,v_i), f_{K^k_{n-k}}(v_1,x)\}\\
&=\epsilon_{K^k_{n-k}}(v_1) \;\; \mbox{(by Lemma \ref{lem14}(i)).}
\end{align*}
Similarly, it can be shown that $\epsilon_G(v)\leq \epsilon_{K^k_{n-k}}(v)$ for any $v\in V(G)\setminus \{v_1,z\}$ using Lemma \ref{lem14}. Thus $ES(G)< ES(K^k_{n-k})$.

\noindent {\bf Case-II:} $G\notin G^k_n(S)$\\
By Lemma \ref{lem13}, there exists a $G'\in G^k_n(S)$ such that $ES(G)<ES(G')$ and then by Case-I, we have  $ES(G)<ES(G')\leq ES(K^k_{n-k})$. This proves the result.
